selectionSummary: Selected for cross-border geographic reach, public safety, economic and humanitarian impact, institutional significance and enduring consequences: Hormuz tanker claims and maritime risk; US nationwide FAA disruption and continuing cancellations; COP31 climate negotiations at their midpoint. A reasoned editorial selection, not an absolute ranking.

snapshot.summary: Iran reported three fresh tanker mine incidents as the UN warned about civilian shipping in Hormuz; international and domestic air travel continued suffering from a nationwide FAA ground stop; and COP31 climate negotiators faced disputes over fossil fuels and finance while activists marched in Antalya.
connections: Both the Hormuz maritime confrontation and US air-traffic outage jeopardized globally connected transport systems, through very different military and technical mechanisms.
War-driven energy insecurity affected worldwide transport and intersected with COP31 debates about electrification and energy investment without making the events causally identical.
Military, corporate and government statements across these stories require independent corroboration before they are accepted as proven outcomes.
uncertainties: Vessel identities, mine causation and crew conditions in Saturday's reported Strait of Hormuz incidents were not verified.
The FAA's final technical root cause, full cancellation impact and actual Sunday restoration were unsettled.
COP31 had not resolved fossil-fuel transition terms, implementation mechanisms or adaptation-finance commitments.

stories.title: Iran reports three tanker fires near Hormuz as UN warns of seafarer risks
stories.summary: Iranian state outlets reported that three oil tankers caught fire on November 14 after allegedly striking mines in or east of the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters could not independently verify the incidents, and the vessels and any casualties were unidentified. Separately, a UN official had told the Security Council that 25 seafarers died in maritime security incidents in the region since February.
stories.whyItMatters: A global oil-and-gas shipping corridor faces elevated danger during the US-Iran conflict. Risks to civilian crews, international shipping, freight, energy security and prices reach far beyond the Gulf.
stories.region: Strait of Hormuz / Iran / Persian Gulf
stories.selectionRationale: Commercial shipping risks at a globally important energy chokepoint, plus direct humanitarian exposure and geopolitical escalation, justify selection.
stories.evidenceNote: Three distinct original newsroom reports on Nov14 independently document the Iranian allegation; none independently proves that mines hit three actual vessels. AP is a same-day Middle East news roundup with a dedicated Hormuz section, disclosed instead of implying it is a standalone tanker report. Al Jazeera attributes 25 seafarer deaths to a UN Security Council briefing. Original initial clocks for AP and Al Jazeera were not verified; no archive capture exists.

commonFacts.text: On November 14 Iranian officials claimed that three oil tankers caught fire after striking mines near the Strait of Hormuz; corroboration establishes only that authorities made the claim.
Iranian naval officials linked the alleged incidents to routes they considered unauthorized and threatened further vessels using those routes.
The available reports did not give independently verified identities, casualty information or damage assessments for all three purported vessels.

framingDifferences.text: Reuters stresses the absence of independent evidence for the mine strikes; Al Jazeera emphasizes the humanitarian and commercial shipping risks described by the UN.
AP's regional roundup situates the tanker claims amid other conflict and civilian-harm reports, unlike Al Jazeera's specialist maritime safety focus.

uncertainties: Whether the mine strikes and tanker fires occurred as the Iranian military described.
Names, registration and destinations of vessels; crew injuries, rescue and actual physical damage.
Future vessel passage, security guarantees and repercussions for oil, insurance and freight prices.

stories.title: US aviation recovery stalls after nationwide FAA communications disruption
stories.summary: Thousands of US flights remained canceled or delayed on November 14 as airlines recovered from a nearly five-hour nationwide FAA ground stop on Friday. Transport officials attributed the problem to equipment upgrades that overloaded aviation communications networks, but whether hardware fault or installation error was responsible remained under investigation. FAA chief Bryan Bedford expected recovery by late Sunday.
stories.whyItMatters: US airspace is central to international passenger, cargo and business travel. Cascading flight disruption and possible faults in aging control systems expose systemic operational and oversight risks.
stories.selectionRationale: An exceptionally rare national flight shutdown in a major global aviation hub triggered multi-day domestic and cross-border economic disruption.
stories.evidenceNote: Reuters, Associated Press and Guardian report independently from November 14. The Reuters live-updated page contains counts as of 9:35pm Eastern on Saturday, equal to 02:35 UTC November 15, AFTER the Paris cutoff; those post-cutoff figures are excluded, and only common pre-cutoff statements are used. Guardian was first published and updated Nov14 before the Paris cutoff. AP's first-release clock was not exposed.

stories.title: COP31 enters final negotiating week with fossil-fuel disputes and climate protests
stories.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, UN climate chief Simon Stiell urged delegates on November 14 to avoid tactical delay as negotiators entered their second week. Australian lead negotiator Chris Bowen described constructive but unfinished work on finance, just transition and electrification. Climate demonstrators, including Turkish LGBTQ+ activists concerned about restrictions on public expression, marched in the host city. No final text was agreed.
stories.whyItMatters: An agreement among nearly all countries could shape emissions, energy investment and resilience funding globally; civil-society participation also matters to accountability and legitimacy.
stories.selectionRationale: A global multilateral summit addressing decade-scale climate and energy policy, finance and human welfare has enduring cross-border impacts.
stories.evidenceNote: Reuters and Anadolu published separate Nov14 reporting from negotiating briefings; Guardian's independently reported march broadens coverage beyond official positions. A stated need for compromise does not establish success or a final deal. Bowen's optimism and demonstrators' accounts are attributed. Reuters displays a possibly updated timestamp without a verified first release time. No archive captures.

UN climate executive Simon Stiell publicly urged delegates to address difficult issues promptly and avoid tactical delays.
